title: Phased model-variant deprecation and migration playbook (catalog v2 -> v3)
creator: Ava Chen
description: Playbook to coordinate a phased deprecation of model-catalog v2 model variants in favor of catalog v3 variants. Covers migration guidance for SDK and API consumers, console UX banners, release notes, enterprise outreach, and cross-team rollout tasks. Goal: retire v2-variant namespace with minimal customer disruptions, provide tooling and clear timelines for automated migration, and ensure telemetry to detect regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Public deprecation announcement published and linked from Console within scheduled window
Migration guide published and validated with 3 sample customers (low/medium/high usage)
SDKs (Python, TS) include clear deprecation warnings and automated codemods for common patterns
Runtime has fallback policy implemented to route v2 requests to compatible v3 variant for 60 days post-deprecation
Monitoring dashboards show no >10% error regression in first 14 days after migration starts
Enterprise customers with dedicated capacity have bespoke migration plans scheduled and acknowledged
tasks: Docs: produce migration guide (API diffs, sample code, token/cost implications)
Engineering: implement 2-phase fallback routing (canary then global) - ENG-2348
SDK: add deprecation header warning + helper to pin compatible v3 variant - SDK-507
Design: create Console banner variants, deprecation modal, and in-product checklist
CS: segment customers by usage patterns and prepare outreach sequences (email + CSM calls)
Legal: review deprecation language for enterprise contracts
Comms: prepare blog post, status page entry, and changelog copydeck
Release: coordinate release notes across runtime, SDKs, and Console (one combined RN)
rollout_timeline: 2026-03-17: Finalize public timeline & publish internal playbook
2026-03-24: Docs + migration guide v1 published (internal review)
2026-04-07: SDK deprecation warnings released (alpha) and codemod preview
2026-04-14: Console banners + in-product checklist deployed to beta orgs
2026-04-28: Begin canary fallback routing (1% traffic to fallback) - monitor 7d
2026-05-12: Expand fallback routing to 25% if no regressions
2026-05-21: Enterprise outreach complete; migration assistance for high-impact customers scheduled
2026-06-20: Target retirement of v2 variant namespace (soft shutdown; 30-day emergency rollback window)
2026-07-20: Hard disable of v2 variant namespace (cleanup & billing reconciliation)
communication_plan: Week -6 to 0: Internal comms (all-hands + team-specific sessions) to align on playbook
Week 0: Public blog post + status page notice + in-console banner linking to migration guide
Ongoing: Weekly email digests to affected developer accounts, prioritized by usage tier
CS: high-touch calls for customers >$5k/month, bi-weekly migration office hours
SDK changelog: clear deprecation section with code samples and codemod instructions
Social/Marketing: coordinated social posts scheduled after public announcement
Support: updated canned responses, escalation paths, and playbook for on-call engineers
release_notes_summary: Deprecating catalog v2 model variants in favor of catalog v3 variants. Customers should pin v3 variants or use provided fallback during migration. SDKs will surface deprecation warnings and codemods to simplify updates. See migration guide for compatibility and cost guidance.
migration_steps: Audit: run catalog-usage job to list customers using v2 variants (automated script)
Pin: recommend customers explicitly pin to v3 variants where behaviour/cost is identical
Compatibility: enumerate API parameter differences and provide code diffs for common SDK calls
Codemod: provide 1-click codemod for TypeScript and Python that updates variant names and flags
Testing: provide samples and a sandbox org for customers to test outputs and cost delta
Fallback: enable runtime fallback routing for 60 days with telemetry and escalation hooks
Rollback: document emergency rollback steps and SLA with Dedicated customers
risks: Unexpected quality regressions when routing to v3 variants for edge-case prompts
High-volume customers with pinned internal pipelines may miss communications and experience outages
SDK codemod may not cover bespoke usage patterns leading to developer friction
Billing reconciliation errors when variants are removed from catalog
Legal/contract clauses for enterprise customers may restrict automated migrations
related_issues: PM-4721 (deprecation playbook v2 model api sunset)
followups: Post-mortem doc with telemetry highlighting common migration failures
Identify automation to reduce future deprecation friction (e.g., in-console one-click migrate)
Feedback survey to migrated customers and update migration guide v2
notes: Keep messaging developer-first: emphasize sample diffs, cost delta, and rollback options.
Ensure telemetry includes edge-case signal: token distribution, output divergence, latency change
Plan for an extended enterprise-only freeze period if legal approvals delay rollout
